en: Wearing a hat and applying sunscreen protects your skin from harmful ultraviolet rays when the UV index is high.
Boiling floodwater for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria and prevents diseases like leptospirosis after a typhoon.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground and taking cover under a sturdy desk protects you from falling debris.
Washing your hands after playing in soil removes harmful bacteria that can cause infections if they enter a cut.
Washing rocks before using them in an aquarium removes harmful minerals and dirt that could make your fish sick.
Eliminating stagnant water around your house stops mosquitoes from breeding, which prevents the spread of dengue fever.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without special glasses can permanently damage your retinas and cause blindness.
Finding the North Star, or Polaris, helps you determine true north if you get lost outdoors at night.
Knowing that a full moon causes higher tides helps beachgoers avoid getting trapped by sudden rising water.
If you hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning, so you must go indoors immediately.
Wearing layered clothing traps body heat and prevents hypothermia when temperatures drop significantly during the cold dry season.
Wearing an N95 mask during a volcanic eruption filters out fine ash particles and protects your lungs from damage.
